articles.title: EIA Edges 2026 USA Oil Output Forecast Closer to 14MM Bpd
articles.description: The U.S. Energy Information Administration further raised its U.S. crude oil production forecast for 2026 in its latest short term energy outlook.

articles.title: EQT, Range Resources to merge in $50bn all-stock deal
articles.description: EQT has agreed to acquire rival Appalachian Basin producer Range Resources in an all-stock transaction that would create a US natural gas entity with a pro forma enterprise value of more than $50bn.

articles.description: Michel Teughels considers what happens when innovative technologies must scale, and how long-term strategies can remain flexible.

articles.title: Asia to dominate global PET capacity growth through 2030
articles.description: Growing consumption of PET in packaging and textile industries is driving capacity additions in the region.

articles.title: Israeli Power Producer Launches Arbitration vs Chevron's Leviathan Partners
articles.description: Dalia Energies has sought arbitration in London over a 20-year natural gas supply agreement terminated by NewMed Energy and Ratio Energies, Chevron's local partners in the offshore Leviathan field.

articles.title: bp and Louisiana resolve outstanding Deepwater Horizon lawsuits
articles.description: bp has agreed to make an early payment of approximately $350m to Louisiana, US and resolve remaining coastal zone lawsuits.

articles.title: India’s BPCL to Cut Russian Oil Imports Due to Higher Prices
articles.description: Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL), one of the biggest Indian state-owned refiners, will reduce its purchases of crude oil from Russia in November as high freight costs and premiums for Russia’s crude undermine the attractiveness of Moscow’s oil compared to Middle Eastern offers. BPCL will buy lower volumes of Russian crude in November as the Middle East grades are more commercially attractive for the company now, BPCL’s head of finance, Vetsa Ramakrishna Gupta, said on Monday, discussing the refiner’s quarterly…

articles.title: Oil India reports new natural gas discovery in Krishna-Godavari Basin
articles.description: Oil India reported the discovery of natural gas in the shallow offshore block KG-DSF/GSKW/2018 within the Krishna-Godavari (KG) Basin, India.

articles.title: Super El Niño May Soften Winter Energy Squeeze
articles.description: We extensively covered the unusually strong El Niño, its weather impacts by region, and the risks this adverse weather poses to crop production and global food inflation. UBS's energy team hosted a call Tuesday with meteorologist James Block to assess El Niño impacts for weather markets. The discussion comes amid a global refining crisis and continued disruptions to Strait of Hormuz energy flows, with European natural gas futures approaching 90 euros per megawatt-hour this week. Block offered some relief to energy consumers…

articles.title: Saudi, Turkish Officials Travel to Iran to Cool Tensions
articles.description: Top security officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey are set to meet Iran's leaders in an effort to defuse tensions and breathe new life into talks aimed at preventing a broader war in the Middle East.

articles.title: IEA’s Birol: Energy Prices Won’t Return to Pre-War Levels in 2027
articles.description: The Middle East conflict has tightened energy markets so much that crude oil, fuel, and natural gas prices are unlikely to return to pre-war levels in 2027, Fatih Birol, executive director of the International Energy Agency (IEA), said on Monday. “I am afraid I don't see any credible pathway that the markets will go next year, where we were before this war has started,” Birol said at the Singapore International Energy Week conference, as carried by Reuters. In a speech at the event, Birol cautioned that energy markets are…

articles.title: Russia's Arctic Oil Shortcut Runs Into a Wall of Ice
articles.description: A group of sanctioned Russian tankers dropped anchor some 1,300 kilometers north of the Arctic Circle in July after getting stuck and hunkered down for a long wait in the frozen waters at the top of the world. Help from two nuclear-powered icebreakers was several days' voyage away. The ships were stuck near the Vilkitsky Strait, a 55-kilometer-wide choke point between the coast of northern Siberia and Bolshevik Island, on Russia's Northern Sea Route (NSR) to China. The Kremlin has heavily invested in the promise that retreating Arctic sea ice opens…

articles.title: Borr Drilling rig sinks during offshore Gabon jacking work
articles.description: Borr Drilling has announced that its Prospector 5 offshore rig sank off the coast of Mayumba, Gabon during the evening of 24 October.

articles.title: Saudi Oil Output Jumps 12.2% to 8 Million Bpd in September
articles.description: Crude oil production in Saudi Arabia rose by 12.2% in September from a month earlier, to reach 8 million barrels per day (bpd), data by Al Rajhi Capital Research cited by TradeArabia showed on Monday. Following the very low levels of crude oil output in the spring and early summer, when all Gulf producers slashed output due to inability to ship crude cargoes via the Strait of Hormuz, production has started to recover as Saudi Arabia boosted ship-to-ship (STS) transfers outside the Strait and redirected most exports through its Red Sea port of Yanbu.…

articles.title: Houthis Claim Attacks on Saudi Arabia’s East-West Oil Pipeline
articles.description: The Iran-backed Houthis on Monday claimed they attacked pumping stations along Saudi Arabia’s East-West onshore oil pipeline, the Kingdom’s key crude export route bypassing the Strait of Hormuz. The Houthis also said they attacked the Riyadh airport amid escalating hostilities between the Iran-aligned movement in Yemen and Saudi Arabia. As of early Monday, Saudi Arabia had not confirmed any attacks on the oil pipeline, which was down for two weeks in September following drone attacks that damaged pumping stations and halted loadings…

articles.title: U.S. Army Says It Has Helped 1.5 Billion Barrels of Oil Out of Hormuz
articles.description: U.S. forces have helped Persian Gulf producers move more than 1.5 billion barrels out of the Strait of Hormuz since the Iran war began, Adm. Brad Cooper, the commander of U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM), said during a visit to the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday. More than 3,000 commercial vessels have successfully transited the Strait of Hormuz with support from CENTCOM forces over the last six months, the U.S. military said. “We continue to stand shoulder to shoulder with our Gulf partners and the shipping industry,” said Cooper. “This…

articles.title: Europe's Natural Gas Prices Soar to Four-Year High as Winter Looms
articles.description: Europe’s benchmark natural gas price jumped by 2% at opening in Amsterdam on Monday, extending the 7% weekly gain from last week, as concerns mount that the gas withdrawal season has started amid no signs that Qatar’s LNG flows would return anytime soon. The front-month price at the Dutch Title Transfer Facility (TTF), the benchmark for Europe’s gas trading, rose by 2.1% to as much as $107.40 (95.73 euros) per megawatt-hour (MWh) early on Monday, reaching its highest level since 2022. The European natural gas price is now at its…

articles.title: India's Stock Market Feels the Heat From High Oil Prices
articles.description: The latest jump in oil prices has disturbed Indian equities, with both major indices starting the week with losses and 12 out of India’s 16 sectors booking losses, Reuters reported earlier in the day. With Brent crude trading at over $114 per barrel, it is not hard to see why investor sentiment in the world’s third-largest importer of crude is not exactly optimistic, pushing Sensex down by 0.46 today, and Nifty 50 down by 0.5. IT stocks specifically shed 1.1%, the report said. “Concerns over supply disruptions due to escalating…

articles.title: Saudi Arabia Turns to Singapore for Oil Storage
articles.description: Saudi Arabia has struck a deal with the Singaporean government to store crude oil in underground caverns in the city-state, Bloomberg reported today. The report follows the latest Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure over the weekend, which included oil facilities among their targets. The Saudi crude will be stored in the Jurong Rock Caverns, which are part of a petrochemical complex in southern Singapore, with deliveries to the caverns set to begin in the second half of next year. The caverns have a capacity of 1.47 million cu m of crude oil,…

articles.title: Oil Prices Dip but Hold Above $100 as Middle East Supply Threats Mount
articles.description: Crude oil prices began trading with a dip this week but remain significantly elevated as hostilities between Yemen’s Houthis and Saudi Arabia, as well as Iranian attacks on tankers in the Persian Gulf, continue. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $114.42 per barrel, down from over $116 per barrel last week but up from around $60 per barrel at the end of 2025. West Texas Intermediate remained above $100 per barrel, despite the dip from Friday’s close, trading at $100.97 per barrel at the time of writing, down from a 2026…

articles.title: The Pentagon's Rare Earth Deadline Is Almost Here. Is Anyone Ready?
articles.description: For years, the rare earth industry has been talking about January 1, 2027 as the date that changes everything. That date is now less than 75 days away. On January 1, new Pentagon procurement rules take effect that will restrict the use of Chinese-origin rare earth materials in American weapons systems. The restrictions cover the full supply chain, from mining and refining through separation, melting, and production. Every defense contractor currently sourcing rare earth magnets or magnet materials from China will need a compliant domestic alternative.…

articles.title: Asia Is Building the World’s Next $15 Trillion Energy Market
articles.description: The global energy transition is increasingly becoming an Asian story, and Asia is unlikely to follow the path envisioned in Washington or Brussels. The region’s governments will have enormous influence over the future of coal, oil, natural gas, renewables and energy storage. What happens next in Asia will determine whether the transition actually reduces global fossil fuel consumption or simply adds vast amounts of renewable power to an energy system that keeps getting bigger. Asia requires $1 trillion annually in energy investments over…

articles.title: Oil Prices Rise Despite Middle East Export Recovery
articles.description: Reports about recovering oil flows in the Persian Gulf and the Red Sea have dominated headlines over the past couple of weeks. Yet oil prices have only moved higher, suggesting barrel numbers alone are not enough to convince the world everything’s back to normal. It isn’t. According to the latest Kpler numbers, October oil exports out of the Middle East in total are in fact higher than they were before the U.S. and Israel launched their first strikes on Iran at the end of February.
